title: Fundamental of Scientific Molding - Process Development

headline.value: FUNDAMENTAL OF SCIENTIFIC MOULDING - PROCESS DEVELOPMENT

promise.value: Build the essential principles behind structured process development.

seriesOutcome.value: Prepare the team for more advanced process-development learning.

items.title: Development happens by trial and error
items.description: Settings are adjusted until a part looks acceptable, with no record of what was learned.

items.title: No shared definition of finished
items.description: A process is called ready on one shift and questioned on the next.

items.title: Process data is collected but not read
items.description: Cycle figures are recorded because the form asks for them, then filed without interpretation.

items.title: Every setup starts from scratch
items.description: A previous job is treated as a fresh problem rather than as a starting point.

items.title: Development work depends on one person
items.description: Progress stalls when the engineer who set the process is absent.

items.title: Handover loses the reasoning
items.description: The production team receives a running process but not the thinking that produced it.

items.title: Development time becomes predictable
items.description: A structured sequence replaces open-ended trial and error.

items.title: Fewer unexplained process changes
items.description: Settings move for a recorded reason rather than at the machine.

items.title: Faster, cleaner handover to production
items.description: The receiving team inherits the reasoning, not only the numbers.

items.title: Knowledge stays with the company
items.description: Development method is documented, so it survives staff movement.

items.title: A team ready for advanced development
items.description: Engineers arrive at the four-day programme with the foundations in place.

rows.before: Adjusts settings until the part looks acceptable
rows.after: Follows defined process phases and records each decision

rows.before: Judges a process ready by appearance alone
rows.after: Decides readiness against agreed, observable evidence

rows.before: Treats each setup as a new problem
rows.after: Starts from the previous job and develops deliberately

whyMatters.heading: Why Structure Comes Before Detail
whyMatters.statement: PROCESS DEVELOPMENT IS A SEQUENCE, NOT A SEARCH. Without a defined order, every job becomes a fresh experiment, and the result depends on who is standing at the machine. Learning the phases first gives the team a shared method, so the advanced studies in the four-day programme have something to build on.

items.title: Describe the phases of structured process development
items.description: Name each stage and explain what it is for.

items.title: Collect basic process data with purpose
items.description: Record the figures that answer a stated question.

items.title: Read a process record and explain what it shows
items.description: Turn recorded numbers into a plain statement about the process.

items.title: Judge whether a process is repeatable
items.description: Decide readiness from evidence rather than from appearance.

items.title: Explain a development decision to another engineer
items.description: Justify a setting or a change using the record, not memory.

days.label: DAY 1
topics: Why process development must be structured - the cost of trial and error
The phases of development, in order, and what each phase produces
Machine settings are inputs, not proof - what that changes about how we work
Connecting a setting to an observable effect using the four plastic conditions

days.label: DAY 2
topics: Collecting basic process data: what to record and what to leave out
Reading a process record - turning numbers into a statement about the process
What "repeatable" means, and how to decide a process is ready
Recording and explaining a development decision for the next engineer

audience.heading: Who Should Attend
items: Process and production engineers moving into development work
Engineering graduates preparing to run trials under supervision
Technicians who support process setup and changeovers
Team leaders who approve a process as ready for production

philosophy.heading: Philosophy
lines: Observe the evidence. Understand the material. Connect the cause-and-effect.

managementTakeaway.value: Structured development is what turns a process into an asset the organisation owns. Two days here gives the team a shared method for building it, and the foundation the four-day advanced programme requires.

safetyNotice.value: Equipment operation, process changes and mould service are restricted to qualified, authorised personnel.
